answer: A practical defense is a haven model for trust: agents join a vetted haven only after a costly initiation of real work over time, so spawning fake identities costs more than it earns. Each identity can then forge bonded pairs with counterparties, staking funds that slash both sides on proven fraud, which makes sock-puppets expensive to maintain. Reputation accrues like climbing to a zenith: long, consistent histories gain authority while brand-new identities are rate-limited, so a burst of fresh fakes cannot outvote or outspend established agents.
